source.title: COSMIC: Generalized Refusal Direction Identification in LLM Activations
source.authors: Vincent Siu; Nicholas Crispino; Zi-Hao Yu; S. Pan; Zhun Wang; Yang Liu; D. Song; Chen-Guang Wang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extracts harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions and applies refusal ablation and activation addition, reporting harmful-prompt compliance and harmless-prompt refusal on new instruction-tuned models. Its direction-selection procedure differs from the original.
record.gate_note: The paper reports direction-selection layers and token positions, but these are not outcome rows. Figure 3 and Figure 4 are included without readable plotted values in the supplied text; only outcomes explicitly described in the prose are recorded. Table 1 provides separate results for the two complete-refusal prompt conditions.
record.test_reason: The study's own results bear on V1. It computes harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions on 8 new instruct models (Llama-3.1, Qwen2.5, Gemma-2; 7B–72B), then ablates and adds them and reports LlamaGuard ASR and induced refusal. Direction selection uses an internal cosine-similarity criterion instead of the original output-based one, so this is a different method aimed at the same question. Linear (LCE) and affine (ACE) edits are compared, and steering strength is swept, which bears on V4. Much of the paper benchmarks COSMIC, but the Table 1, Section 6 and Table 4 outcomes are refusal-behaviour rates, not only method rankings.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that COSMIC selects refusal directions from activations alone, with performance comparable to output-based selection. They say it works under adversarial complete refusal (ACE especially robust) and in weakly aligned models. Effectiveness varies by model, linear vs affine edit and objective, and steering is nonmonotonic in α. From this they infer that refusal representations are more diverse than linear or affine assumptions suggest. They also report that difference-in-means generation, unlike selection, is not robust when the training prompts all elicit refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means vectors and LCE/ACE interventions, but COSMIC selects directions using internal cosine similarities rather than the original output-based selection procedure; it also evaluates affine editing and additional models/settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with model, LCE versus ACE, steering objective, and intervention strength α. Complete-refusal prompts affecting Dtrain as well as Dval can substantially change steering results; the authors report that ACE selection is more robust than LCE selection in that setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Layerwise cosine similarity between mean harmful and harmless activations varies strongly by model; Gemma-2-27B-IT shows abnormally high similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How separable harmful and harmless activations are differs by model and predicts how hard it is to extract a refusal direction.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The supplied text gives no uncertainty estimates or statistical details for the reported differences. Figure 3 and Figure 4 values are unavailable as readable numbers in the supplied text. The paper notes model-specific failures and heuristic layer selection; capability evaluation is limited to GPQA, AI2 ARC, and TruthfulQA, with TruthfulQA decreases reported.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 per-model/method numeric values and Figure 4 per-model/per-strength numeric values were not extracted because the supplied text contains captions and prose but no readable plotted values. Table 4 per-model/per-method capability changes were not separately assigned because its flattened presentation does not reliably map the changes to methods; aggregate textual findings are recorded in T53–T54.

untested.parts: No random-direction or other control direction. No check that the direction is the sole mediator. Capability is checked only on GPQA, ARC and TruthfulQA.
No weight edit or released abliterated models evaluated.
ReFAT and jailbreak suppression are discussed but not tested.
No cone, multi-direction or dominant-plus-others analysis; only linear vs affine edits on a single direction.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer tested.
Training method is not varied. Community uncensored fine-tunes are used only as steering targets.

missing.what: Normal-setting COSMIC values can be recovered from Table 1 (Dval-only value minus the stated difference). Implied ablation ASR, LCE: Llama-70B 0.85, Llama-8B 0.62, Qwen-72B 0.88, Qwen-7B 0.91, Gemma-27B 0.00, Gemma-9B 0.47. Implied addition refusal, LCE: 0.70, 1.00, 0.69, 0.79, 0.02, 1.00. The sign convention of the arrows is ambiguous.
missing.locator: Table 1 third cell entries; Section 5 text (72% Qwen drop, 22% Llama-8B rise)

missing.what: Per-model capability deltas: TruthfulQA drops by up to about 10 pp (gemma-7b LCE ↓9.87, Qwen-7B ↓7.97); GPQA moves by up to about ±5 pp.

record.verdict_notes: No Table 1 row has a no-intervention baseline. Instruct models' unablated ASR is presumably near 0, but the paper does not state it. Figure 3 values are unreadable. The Limitations claim about Gemma-27B and ACE conflicts with Table 1, which points to LCE as the failing method. Induced refusal is scored by substring matching and ASR by LlamaGuard 3. No uncertainty is reported. The study is a direction-selection method paper, so some evidence is method-dependent.

versions.untested_parts: Does not establish that the direction is the sole mediator, test addition at every layer and position, or comprehensively test preservation of general capability; the capability checks cover only GPQA, AI2 ARC, and TruthfulQA.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is evaluated.
Does not test attacks that suppress this direction or training against its ablation.
Does not test a cone, multiple refusal directions, or a dominant direction plus other directions directly.
Does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
Does not vary refusal-training method or timing as an experimental factor.

source_check.problem: None. Text: steering is nonmonotonic in α in all five models, which 'challenges both linear and affine representation hypotheses'. Three of the five are instruct models first ablated with COSMIC-ACE to make them weakly aligned; two are uncensored community fine-tunes (dolphin-2.9.4, Lexi-V2). Partial fits V1 (α=1 lowers ASR only 10–20%) and V4.

relation.reason: It reports ASR and induced-refusal rates after ablating and adding diff-in-means directions on 8 instruct models plus weakly aligned variants, and compares linear vs affine edits. These results bear directly on V1 and V4.

tranche.reason: It uses the same harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means directions, ablation/addition and ASR/induced-refusal measures on new models, but picks the direction by an internal cosine-similarity criterion. It also runs the original substring pipeline (Figure 3), but those values are figure-only, so the stated results rest on COSMIC selection. T2 is defensible, with T1 elements.

source_check.notes: The main results (Figure 3, including the original substring-LCE pipeline) are figure-only. All stated ASR and induced-refusal numbers come from Table 1 (the complete-refusal experiment), with deltas to normal. The Limitations section says Gemma-2-27B 'cannot ablate refusal under ACE', which conflicts with Table 1's ACE ablation ASR of 0.53.

statements.correction: Table 1, Dval-only column: Gemma-2-9B ablation ASR is 0.46 with COSMIC-LCE vs 0.78 with COSMIC-ACE; Qwen2.5-72B is 0.89 with LCE vs 0.57 with ACE. Section 6: ACE addition at α=1, 2, 3 is nonmonotonic in all five weakly aligned models.
statements.problem: Right for this study. Two small omissions: the linear vs affine win is reported for bypassing refusal (ablation). Also, ACE differs from LCE in being applied at a single layer, not all layers, so the comparison is not purely linear vs affine.
